- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (±0.30+), reduce forecast magnitude by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
